tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

# Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

**Output Range:** `rect_key` in `[0, 2^32)`, unique and stable across attach, detach, restore and animation (an attach renumbers nothing); a leaf with `leaf_w = 0`, an inactive variant slot and a zero-length variant slot keep their `idx` and their keys are skipped. Lint `RECT_INDEX_DENSE` checks the union of **static, leaf and variant** indices is exactly `0 … N−1`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

**Example:** `fixture_cryo_excerpt` static rects, sorted: idx 0 N wall `[24, 408) × [72, 96)`; idx 1 W wall `[24, 48) × [96, 384)`; idx 2 heater `[240, 336) × [96, 144)`; idx 3 E wall `[384, 408) × [96, 384)`; idx 4 S wall west `[24, 240) × [384, 408)`; idx 5 S wall east `[336, 408) × [384, 408)` — `N_static = 6`, so `door_cryo_s` has leaf `idx = 6`; in section 3 its `rect_key = 3 × 4096 + 6 = 12,294`. A half-open query box `[380, 400) × [100, 112)` gives `cx0 = 7`, `cx1 = floor_div(399, 48) = 8`, `cy0 = 2`, `cy1 = floor_div(111, 48) = 2`, so 2 cells; **at a cell edge** `[96, 144) × [0, 48)` touches exactly cell column 2 (`cx1 = floor_div(143, 48) = 2`) and `[96, 145) × [0, 48)` touches columns 2 and 3. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Socket slots (two fixtures):** `fixture_socket_w2` (an E-facing socket, `line_px` 696, `start_px` 240, `W` 2, on a run that is exactly the span, one hatch door) has `N_static` 0, `N_doors` 1, so LEAF `idx` 0, PLATE `idx` 1, JAMB `idx` 2 (zero-width, omitted in every state); `fixture_socket_w3` (the same socket with `W` 3 on the run `[672, 696) × [192, 432)`) has static rects `[672, 696) × [192, 240)` (`idx` 0, before the span) and `[672, 696) × [384, 432)` (`idx` 1, after it), so `N_static` 2, LEAF `idx` 2, PLATE `idx` 3 (`[672, 696) × [240, 384)`), JAMB `idx` 4 (`[672, 696) × [336, 384)`, 48 px). In section 3 the `fixture_socket_w3` PLATE key is `3 × 4096 + 3 = 12,291`. A 16 × 8 foot box moving 3 px per tick sweeps at most a 22 × 14 box (D.22), which touches at most 4 cells.

### D.10 Hash and canonical bytes

The layout hash formula is defined as:

`geometry_hash = low32( H64( canonical_geometry_bytes ) )` · `visual_hash = low32( H64( canonical_visual_bytes ) )` (the two halves of the former `template_hash`, LY-26 e; *Amended 2026-10-27 — design review*) · `layout_hash = block_hash(&"layout.state") = H64( canonical_bytes( layout.state snapshot ) )` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)*. `canonical_bytes` is the kernel's prefix-free TLV form (kernel D.12); Layout owns the snapshot SHAPE only (the AC-130 allow-list, arrays in ascending id order, tombstones retained, derived caches `version`, grids, leaf cache, PROJECTOR objects and `mutation_count` excluded) and writes no byte encoder for the block. `layout_hash()` calls the kernel read `block_hash(&"layout.state", uncached = true)` (new, kernel request K-2), which exists in every build because Horror HE-25 keys its path cache on it in release. The two template-local byte strings `canonical_geometry_bytes` and `canonical_visual_bytes` (and only those) are `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` per field in a fixed documented order (ADR-LAY-06); they are never compared with a kernel value

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `H64` | function | 64-bit | the kernel's H64 (kernel D.12 and Tuning Knobs `H64`/`mix64` row; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling X13 / R-17): the first 8 bytes, little-endian, of SHA-256 computed with Godot's `HashingContext`; native, no GDScript byte loop *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* | one hash for the whole project |
| `canonical_geometry_bytes` | bytes | template-sized | template | rooms by `room_key` with `origin_px` and tile runs, rects in D.9 order, socket and door positions, hardpoint cells, anchor polylines; strings as length-prefixed UTF-8 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `canonical_visual_bytes` | bytes | small | template | kit-piece ids, art references, dialect, labels *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `canonical_bytes( layout.state )` | bytes | tens of bytes to tens of KB | the kernel's TLV encoder (kernel D.12) over the block snapshot | counters, bodies, instances, sockets, welds; Layout supplies the snapshot shape only *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: ruling consequence of X13 / R-17, kernel D.12)* |
| `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash` | u32 each | `[0, 2^32)` | persisted per instance | drift gate (LY-26 e) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| hash cadence | policy | n/a | this GDD | see Output Range *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |

(a) *Seam.* `occluder_source(body_id) -> OccluderSource` exposes `rects_in(aabb)` and `version(section_id)` with EM-20's names verbatim (names unchanged; the out parameter of LY-12 e and the sibling `static_version` / `leaf_version` are additive). EM-20 names no `body_id` while EM-30 compares geometry only within one body, so each instance's `rects_in` answers in THAT body's frame, in ascending key `(section_id, idx)` (D.9) — the **reserved key set** is stable across a weld, a cut and a restore because an attach renumbers nothing: every piece that can ever exist at a socket (PLATE, JAMB, LEAF; LY-15) owns an `idx` from the template's compile, and a state change only switches slots between active and inactive (an inactive slot is omitted from results exactly like a `leaf_w` 0 rect). What changes on a weld is therefore the *active subset* of the sockets' slots, never a key. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
(b) *Boundary convention — stated once.* Integer coordinates in Layout name pixel CELLS. A stored rect `[x0, x1) × [y0, y1)` therefore *occupies* cells `x0..x1−1`, `y0..y1−1`. **One convention per function, no exceptions** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: every box a caller passes IN (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`'s foot boxes, D.2, D.9, D.22) is **half-open** `[ax0, ax1) × [ay0, ay1)`; every rect handed OUT by `rects_in` **and by `solid_in`** is the **occupied span** `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, so the Emitter's D.6 slab arithmetic is unchanged in code and Body's cell sweep reads the same numbers. (The earlier D.9 "closed query box" is retired; a half-open box of width `w` starting at `ax0` touches cells `floor_div(ax0, c)` to `floor_div(ax0 + w − 1, c)`.) Rule text: "the conservative closed test (EM-20 a, a graze blocks) is applied to the occupied span `[x0, x1−1] × [y0, y1−1]`; `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` is Chebyshev distance from that span" (D.2). A cell outside every occupied span — the first legal row south of a wall, Pipeline D.12 — is therefore not blocked at its origin, which is what EM-6's "outside every footprint by construction" (EM:157) assumes. The foot box's vertical placement is Body's; Layout's guarantee is stated on rectangles and on whatever box the caller passes: a box whose cells lie outside every occupied span is legal.
**CONFLICT C-1 (one-pixel example, not a rule change; routed to the Emitter owner):** EM:467 (D.6 example), EM:1013 (AC-22) and EM:1014 (AC-23) describe "wall x 408..432" as 25 closed points and reject an anchor at 432; under this rule the wall occupies 408..431, so (432, 200) passes with clearance 1 and (431, 200) fails; AC-22's three probes (540 blocked, 407 clear, 408 blocked) are unchanged. `ANCHOR_CLEARANCE_PX` is confirmed at 1 (range 1-2) and re-sourced to this GDD (Cross-References).
(c) *Broadphase.* A per-body uniform grid, cell `BROADPHASE_CELL_PX` 48, derived, never persisted, rebuilt at build, attach, detach and restore (D.9). One structure serves Body's `solid_in`, the Emitter's segment test and Lighting; the Emitter's ADR candidate 4 ("the broadphase … and whether the spatial index lives in Layout or here", EM:32) is answered: **Layout**. `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` is sized to the Controller's performance criterion (PCI:1078: 2,000 rects, ≤ 0.05 ms per actor per tick at P99; spike, GDScript cost [UNV]). Callers issue ONE `solid_in` per actor per tick with the swept bounding box and sweep analytically against the result, never one query per 1-px step. Rejected: an Emitter-owned index (drift, double memory) and engine physics queries (EM-20: nondeterministic).
(d) *`version(section_id)`* is a monotone u32, NOT persisted, reset to 1 on `restore` (the Emitter rebuilds in its own `post_restore`; consumers must treat a restore as an unconditional rebuild signal, because a post-restore `version` can numerically equal a pre-restore cached value). It is bumped by `build_section`, `attach_section`, `detach_section`, `discard_section_geometry`, `layout.doors` and Layout's own `post_restore` (LY-26 c, 1 → 2 for a section with an open leaf). MVP has no prop mutator (props are static); the bump list is closed so a Vertical Slice movable prop adds one entry deliberately. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Which sections are bumped (the rule, stated once):** every section whose rect set can change is bumped, *moved or not*. That is (i) every section whose **socket state changes** — both sections of the seam on a weld and on a cut, including the host section that does not move, because on a weld its PLATE becomes JAMB plus LEAF and on a cut its LEAF (possibly open, `area` > 0) becomes a solid PLATE, so a consumer keyed on `version` that missed the unmoved mate would keep passing light through a solid plate (a see-through-but-solid wall, the failure the secondary design test forbids); and (ii) every section whose body-frame offset changes (every moved section). Each such section also gets the dirty key `SEC/<id>`, and both bodies of the seam get `BODY/<id>` (LY-16, LY-17, LY-27). **Three counters, one contract** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: `static_version(s)` is bumped by every cause above except a leaf change; `leaf_version(s)` is bumped only by `layout.doors` (and by `post_restore`'s self-heal for an open leaf); `version(s)` is the EM-20 name and is bumped whenever either is, so a consumer that rebuilds everything keys on `version` unchanged, while a consumer that can patch (the Emitter's static layer, the weld-preview memo) keys the static layer on `static_version` and the dynamic leaves on `leaf_version`. Animating a door therefore bumps `static_version` 0 times; a stepped slide (a Vertical Slice option, OQ-14 c) costs a leaf patch per tick, never a full static rebuild. All three are not persisted and reset to 1 on `restore`. **`changed_region(section_id)`** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*: a pure ordered read `changed_region(section_id) -> ALL | REGION(box) | FRAME`, valid for bumps applied in the current tick (cleared at the end of the tick; the Emitter reads it in W0 of the same tick, because `emitter.place` runs every tick after the P2 apply; NONE when no bump was applied to the section this tick); derived, never persisted (after a restore every section reports ALL once; `version` already resets to 1). Values: build, discard and `post_restore` = ALL (unchanged); a `layout.doors` leaf change = REGION(union box of the old and new leaf rectangles; Emitter ask E-N, unchanged); `attach_section` (LY-16) and `detach_section` (LY-17): for each of the two socket-host sections REGION(union box of that socket's PLATE, JAMB and LEAF slot rectangles, active and inactive, in the section's body frame); for every other moved section (the absorbed body's remaining sections, or the cut-off component's remaining sections) FRAME = a pure translation of the whole body (`rot_q` 0), geometry and slot sets unchanged. A socket-host section that also moves reports REGION; a reader detects its translation by comparing `section_offset(section_id)` with its cached value. The bumps of `version` and `static_version` are unchanged. The read tells the Emitter what kind of change a `static_version` bump was, so it can re-derive its `body_id` and keep its pair rows across a weld or cut without a full cold rebuild (Emitter S8 against S8b); a reader that does not read it treats every bump as ALL.
(e) *Allocation and the result contract.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The hot-path API is an **out-parameter** API: `rects_in(aabb, out: QueryBuffer)` and `solid_in(body_id, aabb, out: QueryBuffer)` fill a **caller-owned** `QueryBuffer` and return the record count; they return no array. A function that returned one shared reused buffer would alias between consumers (Body's sweep, the Emitter, Lighting and Interaction's throw all call within one tick) and cannot be both allocation-free and safe under copy-on-write, so each consumer owns one buffer and `clear()` resets its length without releasing capacity. **Record layout (structure of arrays, one index per record):** `keys: PackedInt64Array` — `rect_key = section_id × RECT_KEY_STRIDE + idx` reaches `2^32 − 1`, which overflows a 32-bit element for `section_id >= 2^19`, so the key column is 64-bit; `spans: PackedInt32Array` — four ints per record `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, the occupied span in the BODY frame (LY-12 b); `flags: PackedByteArray` — one LY-7 flags byte. Records are in ascending `rect_key`; a rect appears once per call (the broadphase de-duplicates a rect spanning several cells). A value-returning wrapper (`rects_in_copy`) may exist for tools and tests only and is not on a hot path. The steady-state call allocates nothing once each buffer has reached its working capacity. (→ ADR: packed-array buffer layout and the engine cost of `resize`, spike SP-ENG-1.)

### 4. Template identity, the ledger nesting (OQ-B) and the three hashes (ADR-LAY-04, -06)

**Ledger nesting (ADR-0007 OQ-B).** `assets/data/sections/ids.lock.json` is one `section_templates` space with one flat `pairs[]`, exactly the shape ADR-0007 § 3.2 defines, so `LedgerCheck.verify` stays generic and the append-only CI gate needs no second format. Two classes share the space, told apart by **key shape**: a template pair has key `<template_id>`, a room pair has key `<template_id>/<room_key>` (the `/` is illegal inside a snake_case key, so the split is unambiguous). Template ids come from the low part of the declared range and room ids from above a fixed boundary (a `SectionLedgerCheck` in `src/data/sections/`, owned by Layout by review, checks the boundary, that every room pair's prefix is a template pair in the same ledger, and that retiring or dormanting a template does the same to its room pairs: lint `LEDGER_ROOM_ORPHAN`). One entry per `room_key` rather than a nested list keeps `dormant` and `retired_ids` per room, so removing one room from a template is a per-pair `dormant` flip and a renamed room is a visible new pair, which is the diff a migration step needs. The integers are **not persisted in `layout.state`** (the instance persists the `template_id` string, § 2); they exist so a rename or removal after `SHIPPED` is detected and migrated (ADR-0007 § 3.3), and so later blocks can reference a room by integer if they must.

**The three hashes (the shape of ADR-LAY-06).** ADR-0005 § 3.1 forbids an owner-written `[u32 tag][u32 length][payload]` byte string, and § 4.6 already defines the template hashes as `Hash64.of_value` of a post-cast sub-payload "whose shape is Layout's and ADR-0013's". So ADR-LAY-06 becomes the **`Dictionary` shape of three sub-payloads**, hashed once by `SectionTemplates` at catalog freeze and stored as `low32` in the template row (never in the template file, ADR-0007 § 3.5):

| Hash | Payload (keys sorted by the encoder, so order in source is irrelevant; every family is one flat `PackedInt32Array` in the field order of its LY-4 row, strings replaced by template-local indices, variable-length members as a CSR `*_off` array plus a data array) | Changes when |
|---|---|---|
| `geometry_hash` | `size_tiles`; `rooms` (origin, flags, tile runs); `wall_runs` (orientation, start, length, kind, flanking rooms, `face_h_px`, `face_variant`); the compiled `rects` (stride 7: `x0, y0, x1, y1, flags, owner_kind, owner_ref`, in `idx` order, leaf and variant slots at their closed or full extent); `doors`; `sockets` with their `lanes`; `hardpoints`; `plate_positions`; `loose_slots`; `story_slots`; `anchors` (polyline CSR); `fixture_anchors`; `instrument_placements` (geometry fields only) | anything that decides where a rectangle, tile, socket, door or anchor is |
| `visual_hash` | `dialect`; kit-piece ids and layers; art references; labels; advisory hints (`socket_tag`); flags no query reads | only presentation changes |
| `structure_hash` | the **ordered** key sequences: `room_key[]`, `socket_key[]`, `door_key[]`, `hp_key[]`, `node_ref[]`, `edge_ref[]`, `anchor_key[]`, `slot_id[]`; each room's sorted tile list | any reorder, add, remove or rename of an identity-bearing element, or any tile-set change |

**Why a third hash.** LY-26 e classifies a template change as "structural" when the *sets* of keys or a room's tile set differ, but the block persists only two hashes, so the check has nothing to compare against except Graph counts. A pure **reordering** (rooms `[a, b]` to `[b, a]`) keeps every set equal and every count equal, yet `room_id = room_id_base + room_index`, `socket_index` and `comp_base + room_index` all index the *current* template by position, so an existing save would silently attach its Graph compartments and welded sockets to the wrong rooms and sockets. LY-6 e's sentence "a template that merely reorders rooms changes ids only for NEW instances" is therefore wrong as written. The remedy is to persist what the check needs: `structure_hash` is one more `int32` per instance (§ 2), costs four bytes a row, and makes the structural rule exact: **a `structure_hash` mismatch is `LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED` for every instance, history or not**, because every instance has Graph data built from the old order. `geometry_hash` keeps the GDD's history-dependent rule (§ 10). The third hash is not redundant with `geometry_hash`: because `rooms` are encoded in declaration order, a reorder already changes `geometry_hash`, which on an instance **with history** is refused by the GDD's own rule; the marginal value of `structure_hash` is the **never-welded `FREE` instance**, where the history-dependent rule would accept the change as `geometry_changed_fresh` and silently re-point `room_id_base + room_index`, `comp_base + room_index` and `socket_index` to the wrong rooms and sockets. This is a deliberate deviation from the TR text "13-int section-instance rows" (the row is 14 columns, one of them the string); it is listed first among the decisions for the user's review.

**Two more template rules.** (a) Every coordinate of a footprint rectangle, socket `line_px`/`start_px`, room `origin_px` and wall run lies on the 24-px grid (`WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`) except a door leaf's moving edge (LY-3 a, LY-7); `GRID_24` is a **BOOT invariant** (`CONTENT_INVARIANT`, ADR-0007 § 2.4), not only a CI lint, because the closure of the weld offset on the grid (§ 7) and the broadphase cell alignment depend on it; a 12-px shift in a socket fails the load (TR-derelict-033 Layout half). (b) `area_max <= 0` on a door is the one named structural invariant D.5 needs (it divides by it) and refuses the load; the published `area_max` range is guidance (ADR-0007 § 2.5). (c) `area_max <= width_px` (the 96-px door cell) is a second `CONTENT_INVARIANT` (ruling CT-14). It is a numeric bound between `area_max` in flow units (ADR-0011 § 2.1: 64 = one standard door) and `width_px` in pixels, with no unit conversion implied: the leaf gap `floor_div(width_px * area, area_max)` is a dimensionless ratio that never exceeds `width_px` (the leaf is never wider than the doorway it closes), and the bound guarantees that one flow unit opens at least one pixel, so `open_extent_px > 0` exactly when `area > 0` (ADR-0034 OQ-E) and the jamb/leaf extents stay inside the doorway.

### 6. Sockets, seams and the mating predicate

- **A socket is a pre-declared attachment site** `{socket_key, facing N|E|S|W, line_px, start_px, width_tiles, class_id, lanes[], hatch | none}` in the template (LY-13). `pos_px` is `(line_px, start_px)` for E/W facings and `(start_px, line_px)` for N/S. The four-facing footprint, LOW-end, PLATE/JAMB/LEAF table of LY-13 is normative and is not restated.
- **States (TR-section-018, TR-assembly-025).** `FREE -> WELDED(seam_id) -> CAPPED` (after a SEALED cut) or `CUT_OPEN` (after a RAGGED cut); `CAPPED` and `CUT_OPEN` never return to `FREE` in MVP, which supports exactly one weld-then-cut cycle per socket. **A socket's state is written only inside LM2 and LM3.** There is no `install_cap_plate`, no `set_socket_state` and no setter on `LayoutState.sockets`; `socket_state` writes are private to `weld_math`/`detach_planner` helpers called by those two mutators, and a lint (`LAY-SOCKET-01`, tier E1, ADR-0010 § 6) rejects any other write to the `sockets` columns.
- **`can_attach` is a pure, first-failure-wins reason chain** (TR-section-019), cheap before expensive, in this fixed order: `SOCKET_UNKNOWN`, `SOCKET_NOT_FREE`, `SAME_BODY`, `FACING_MISMATCH`, `WIDTH_MISMATCH`, `CLASS_MISMATCH`, `LANE_MISMATCH`, `COORD_LIMIT`, `GEOM_OVERLAP`. `COORD_LIMIT` (ruling CT-24) refuses a weld whose resulting body-frame extent (the survivor's sections plus the absorbed sections at `offset_b`, from `weld_math`, no geometry test) would exceed `BODY_COORD_LIMIT`, the bound ADR-0015 defines in `BodyTuning` and its bounds ledger (at most 2^24) and which Layout reads from the same `ScalarTable` value through `LayoutTuning`, never from `body.state`; it is cheap integer arithmetic, so it precedes `GEOM_OVERLAP`. `SAME_BODY` being a hard reject and every weld merging two bodies is what makes the weld relation a **forest** and a cut always split a body into exactly two components.
- **`GEOM_OVERLAP`.** The test set is the static footprint of both bodies after the D.6 translation: every static rect with all flags, each PLATE slot at its full footprint, no leaf and no JAMB slot, plus the tile cells of every room (rect against tile and tile against tile, so a wall over the other body's floor and two floors on one cell both fail); abutting is legal. **The rect-vs-rect leg is ADR-0014's `footprint_overlaps`; the tile-cell leg (rect-vs-tile and tile-vs-tile) is Layout's own `floor_tile_at`-based check, run after `footprint_overlaps` returns no rect hit** (ruling CT-16). The test runs over each body's broadphase handle (ADR-0014) and is **memoised on `(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, static_version_a, static_version_b)`**; uncached cost target <= 2 ms (TR-section-019), a pending-spike figure (V3). The memo is a small fixed-capacity ring in `LayoutDerived`, reset on restore.
- **Slot activation is a pure function** of `(this socket's state, this socket's hatch, the mate's hatch, W)` evaluated by LM1 to LM4 and `post_restore` (the LY-15 matrix); no persisted field is needed because the mate's hatch is known from the two templates. A hatched socket whose mate is bare is `hatch_one_sided`: legal, behaves bulkhead-only, its PLATE stays on while `WELDED`.
- **The `can_attach` preview needs more than a reason**, and a Class A check returns a bare `StringName` (ADR-0003 § 5). So the payload `{reason, hatch_one_sided, openings_count}` is its own pure read, `preview_attach(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: AttachPreview) -> void`, and `can_attach(...)` is `preview_attach` followed by returning `out.reason` (`&""` = OK). One implementation, two shapes.
- **`socket_plan(socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, out: WeldPlan)`** is a pure read that is **canonicalised survivor-first**: it relabels the two arguments through `weld_math.survivor_of` (the survivor rule of § 7, Alternative 9) before filling anything, so the `JoinPlan` the Graph's `weld_join` receives, the `opening_ids` order and the Graph's seam row (`section_a`/`section_b`) are argument-order independent (ruling CT-13; ADR-0011 notes that `weld_join` row order follows the canonical `JoinPlan`). It fills the Graph's weld-plan DATA verbatim (one lane pair per lane in `(loop, lane_index)` order, one opening per mated hatch pair `(comp_a, comp_b, area_max)`, `L_seam = width_tiles`). The field layout of `WeldPlan` follows ADR-0011's `JoinPlan`; Layout fills it, Assembly adds `q`, the Graph's `can_join` validates, and both verdicts must pass before apply.

content.content:
### 2. The snapshot payload: dense parallel columns, ascending ids, tombstones kept

`snapshot(ctx)` calls `ctx.put(payload)` with a `Dictionary` whose keys are `String`s. Every table is a set of **parallel columns** (TR-section-006): no `Dictionary` is keyed by an id, no `Vector2i`/`Rect2i`/`Color`/`Resource`/`StringName`, no `PackedStringArray`, and every packed array in the payload is a `duplicate()` (ADR-0003 snapshot contract; registry `live_reference_in_snapshot_payload`). The key set is closed; the AC-130 allow-list file is regenerated from this table.

| Payload key | Type | Contents (row order) |
|---|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `int` | `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SCHEMA_VERSION` |
| `counters` | `Dictionary` of three `int`s | `next_section_id`, `next_body_id`, `next_room_id` (first allocated id is 1, so `default_state` sets all three to 1) |
| `bodies` | `Dictionary` | `body_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `origin_section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 0 `LIVE`, 1 `DISSOLVED`); ascending `body_id` |
| `instances` | `Dictionary` of 14 columns | `section_id`, `body_id`, `offset_x`, `offset_y`, `room_id_base`, `node_base`, `edge_base`, `comp_base`, `geometry_hash`, `visual_hash`, `structure_hash` (all `PackedInt32Array`); `rot_q`, `discarded` (`PackedByteArray`); `template_id` (`Array[String]`); ascending `section_id` |
| `sockets` | `Dictionary` | `section_id` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_index` (`PackedByteArray`), `state` (`PackedByteArray`: 1 `WELDED`, 2 `CAPPED`, 3 `CUT_OPEN`; `FREE` = 0 is never stored), `seam_id` (`PackedInt32Array`); ascending `(section_id, socket_index)`; only non-`FREE` sockets have a row |
| `welds` | `Dictionary` | `seam_id`, `section_a`, `section_b` (`PackedInt32Array`), `socket_a`, `socket_b`, `state` (`PackedByteArray`; `state`: 0 `ACTIVE`, 1 `CUT_SEALED`, 2 `CUT_RAGGED`), `welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T` (`PackedInt64Array`); ascending `seam_id` |

Decisions inside the shape:

- **Ids are dense ordinals: `section_id == row + 1` and `body_id == row + 1`.** A section or body id is consumed only by the mutator that appends its row, in the same call, so no id exists without a row. Row lookup is then an index, not a map: no `Dictionary` on the read path, no `bsearch` for the common query. Restore verifies the equality (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_COUNTER`). The cost is that a future "reserve an id then maybe not use it" idea is forbidden by this ADR, which is the right pressure (§ Risks R1).
- **`template_id` is a typed `Array[String]` column** (TR-section-004). The alternatives were the ledger integer (rejected: the GDD allow-list, LY-6 b and every restore reason name the string; four templates; saves are disposable pre-release; a human-readable dump matters more than 4 bytes a row) and a `PackedStringArray` (rejected: not on ADR-0006's allow-list). ADR-0006 does not assert that a typed array survives the codec, so **restore never relies on it**: it checks each element with `typeof(v) == TYPE_STRING` (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_SCHEMA` on failure) and fills the typed column with `Array[String].assign(src)` (§ 10).
- **64-bit times are native `PackedInt64Array` columns** (TR-section-006). ADR-0006 § 1.2 item 3 allows full-width `int` and § 1.3 limits the halves convention to values that can reach JSON; `welded_at_T`/`cut_at_T` reach JSON only through the dev `dump-save`, which renders any `int` of magnitude 2^53 or more as a decimal string and `T` is bounded below 2^53. The GDD's two-halves form stays legal and is not used.
- **The three hashes are stored as signed int32 and compared as `value & 0xFFFFFFFF`** (`IntMath.low32`, ADR-0005 P9; probed 2026-10-29). A comparison without the mask is a lint-visible defect (AC-172 c).
- **`rot_q` is a byte column that must be 0.** It is stored so the field exists in schema v1 and a later rotation feature is not a layout change; any nonzero value is `LAYOUT_ROT_UNSUPPORTED` at restore and a boot error in a template that asks for it.
- **`socket_index` is the template's declaration ordinal** of that socket, a `uint8` (MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION never exceeds 8 and is lint-bounded by `MAX_SEAMS_PER_SECTION`). A runtime socket handle is the packed int `SocketRef = (section_id << 4) | socket_index` (`socket_ref.gd`, 24 bits at the section-id ceiling), used as an argument, a memo key and a sort key; it is never persisted.
- **Seam ids are the Graph's.** A `welds` row's `seam_id` is whatever `weld_join` returned; Layout allocates none and treats it as an opaque positive `int32`. After a cut the two sockets keep their `seam_id` (state `CAPPED` or `CUT_OPEN`) because the scar's bead and cap plate are drawn from that history (Pillar 5).
- **The payload size rule holds.** The largest realistic shape (D.21's long campaign) is tens of KB, far under `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES`; `snapshot()` computes the D.21 estimate from row counts and raises the one-shot diagnostic `layout_block_soft_bytes` when it exceeds `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` (GDD Tuning Knobs); the hard ceiling is Save/Load's (TR-section-030).

**Tombstones.** A discarded section keeps its row with `discarded = 1` and its `body_id`; the body it sat on becomes `DISSOLVED`; its `socket` and `welds` rows stay (a surviving mate keeps its `CAPPED`/`CUT_OPEN` history). Ids stay consumed, so nothing is ever reused or renumbered (TR-section-005).

**Output Range:** pass, or a list of leak cells. A `CUT_OPEN` hatch is `SOLID` (LY-15), so a cut can never create a leak. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* With leaves open, the flood walks through each door gap, so the exception set (door gap cells) is exactly the cells of the gap itself and anything reached beyond it is a leak: **a door whose far side is void, or whose wall is an exterior wall, raises `CONTAINMENT_LEAK`** (the vacuum-door case this lint exists to catch). An interior door between two rooms floods into the other room's tile cells, which are allowed.

**Example:** `cryo_bay` has `42 × 4 = 168` room cells; deleting the N wall run lets the flood reach the void north of it: `CONTAINMENT_LEAK` at the first reached cell. With all walls present the flood stays inside the 168 cells plus the doorway's gap cells and, through the open S door, the neighbouring room's tile cells (on `fixture_cryo_excerpt_contained`, the 16 cells of `cryo_south_stub`); on the bare excerpt the same open door lets the flood reach the void south of the gap, which is a `CONTAINMENT_LEAK` by design *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*.

### D.21 Block size estimate

The block size formula is defined as:

`bytes ≈ 4 × ( 13·I + 10·K + 4·S + 3·B + 3 )` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the instance row is 13 ints, one more than before, because `template_hash` is split into `geometry_hash` and `visual_hash`)*

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `I` | int | 0 … live cap + tombstones | the block | instance rows (13 ints each; discarded rows stay as tombstones, LY-19) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* |
| `K` | int | `I − 1` at most per body | the block | weld rows (10 ints: ids, state, two 2-int times) |
| `S` | int | 0 … `8 × I` | the block | non-`FREE` socket rows (4 ints) |
| `B` | int | 1 … | the block | body rows incl. `DISSOLVED` (3 ints) |

**Output Range:** tens of bytes to tens of KB against `MAX_BLOCK_BYTES` 32 MiB (REG:1915); excludes the template-id strings and the snapshot container overhead [UNV].

**Example:** MVP after the one weld (four sections on four bodies, the pod included; the absorbed body's `DISSOLVED` row still counts): `I = 4`, `K = 1`, `S = 2`, `B = 4` → `4 × (52 + 10 + 8 + 12 + 3) = 340` bytes. A long campaign with 24 live and 200 tombstoned sections, 200 weld rows, 400 socket rows and 208 bodies: `4 × (2,912 + 2,000 + 1,600 + 624 + 3) = 28,556` bytes (about 28 KB), still four orders of magnitude below the ceiling; `LAYOUT_BLOCK_SOFT_BYTES` 65,536 raises a diagnostic long before. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*

=== 302
**LY-25 — World construction order.** `build_section(template_id, kind) -> {section_id, body_id}` (LM1, Class A) = allocate ids → record the instance on its own NEW body at `offset_px` (0, 0) (the body frame's origin is its minimum-id section's origin, D.12) → Graph M1 `instantiate_section(section_id, template_id, kind)` (the Graph's own table names the caller "Layout / derelict build, home-ship setup", LSG:180; `kind` is an argument forwarded to M1 and is **not persisted by Layout** — the Graph's section record owns it, LS-17, LSG:174) → store `graph_ref_base` → build the grid → bump `version`. **Every built section starts on its own body, and every multi-section body is produced by welds only** (authored welds in Vertical Slice procgen use `attach_section` with `welded_at_T` 0): there is no "place on an existing body" path, so the weld relation stays a forest (LY-14) and the component split of LY-17 stays exact. **Layout calls NO Emitter or Interaction mutator.** The orchestrating atomic apply — Web Map & Transit's `init_world(world_seed)` per Save/Load SL-18 (SL:255, run in `LOADING` in `restore_after` order under a WriteScope), the only caller of LM1 (the pod is built there once, as one persistent body, and a pod hop builds nothing — Web Map CF-LY; Assembly never discards (MSA-24) and is not an LM1 caller (C11)) — calls, inside one WriteScope and in this fixed order: Layout `build_section` → Emitter E1 `instantiate_section_emitters(section_id)` (its stated caller stays "Assembly / Web Map atomic apply", EM:147) → Interaction `sync_section(section_id)` → PROJECTOR notification *(Web Map & Transit and Interaction are designed; the call order is theirs to repeat)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Layout supplies their data through reads (`subject_anchors`, `loose_slots`, LY-22, LY-23). This keeps `restore_after: []` honest: Layout depends on nothing at restore. The MVP world (home-ship + derelict A + derelict B + the always-dormant pod: four sections on four bodies, registry `mvp_template_roster`) is a data file `assets/data/world/mvp_world.json` consumed by `init_world`; the floor plans in it are Derelict Authoring's. The build is incremental and the PROJECTOR reports ready when its scene content exists; Transit's `ARRIVING` is the fixed-length state `ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS` 45 ticks; the Pipeline, not the sim, holds the black plate for any PROJECTOR lag (a large section may exceed one tick — `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 is a logging threshold, not a cut-off).
=== 305
(a) `restore(data, stored_version, ctx)` validates into scratch (failures via `ctx.fault(LAYOUT_RESTORE_*)`), then replaces the block's contents in place (copy into the existing block object, never replace the object; root rule ADR-0003 section 2) and only on success *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*; an unsupported `stored_version` is a reported failure (`ctx.fault`), never a silent default. The snapshot obeys SL-2 (SL:176): no `Vector2i`, `Rect2`, `Color` or `Resource`; integer vectors travel as two ints or a packed integer array; dictionary keys are String or int; 64-bit values (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`) never travel as JSON numbers (two 32-bit halves or strings remain legal; a native int64 is also accepted in the binary payload, exact; the convention is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON, i.e. the header and the dev dump-save) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Concrete encoding rules** (JSON text turns int keys into strings and numbers into floats; the payload itself is `var_to_bytes` binary, SL-2, but the dev `dump-save` JSON and the generic K-3 round-trip test must not change a table's meaning): (1) **no integer-keyed Dictionary** — every table (instances, sockets, welds, bodies) is a dense set of parallel packed arrays in ascending id order, so a stringified key can never be misread; the few Dictionaries are String-keyed and hold only scalars and packed arrays; (2) **64-bit values** (`welded_at_T`, `cut_at_T`; and `layout_hash` wherever Save/Load's header carries it, which is not `layout.state`, D.10 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*) travel as **two 32-bit int halves** `(hi, lo)` (or exact strings; a native int64 is also exact and legal in the binary payload, so this convention is mandatory only where a value can reach JSON: the header and the dev dump-save; ADR-0006) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*, each normalised with `& 0xFFFFFFFF` before any compare (D.10) — the project convention (Interaction `last_salvage_T`, Assembly `last_shape_change_T`, and D.21's two-int count) — and are rendered as exact-width lowercase hex strings (`Hex64`) **only by Save/Load's header** (SL-2 S-1), never as a JSON number. The dev `dump-save` does **not** use hex: per ADR-0006 section 1.3 item 4 it renders any `int` of magnitude 2^53 or more as a lowercase **decimal string**, and the two halves, being plain ints below 2^32, appear as ordinary ints. Layout stores `welded_at_T` and `cut_at_T` as halves `(hi, lo)` in its snapshot (its choice, not an ADR requirement; the native-int64 form stays legal but is not used), so a dump of `layout.state` shows two plain ints per 64-bit value and no hex string *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix: the earlier dump-as-hex clause contradicted ADR-0006 section 1.3 item 4 and Save/Load L181)*; (3) **`snapshot()` deep-copies**: it returns fresh packed arrays, never a reference into the live block, so a mutation after `snapshot()` cannot reach a captured snapshot (and a captured snapshot cannot be mutated into the live block).

(b) *Class 1 — static queries, valid immediately after `restore()` returns.* Every query that depends only on templates and the instance table — `room_at`, `V`, `exposed_tiles`, `room_surface`, `socket_plan`, `anchor_geometry`, static `rects_in`, `section_offset`, `body_of` — is valid at once, because templates were loaded in BOOTING and the instance table is the only restored state. This makes the Graph's loud failure (`GRAPH_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_ROOM` on mis-order, LSG:831) impossible by construction whatever the order of `post_restore` calls.
(c) *Class 2 — leaf-dependent results, valid only after Layout's own `post_restore()`.* DOOR_LEAF rects depend on the Graph's persisted `area`, which Layout cannot read inside its own `restore()` (the Graph restores after Layout) and which the Graph now publishes as `opening(edge_id) -> {area, area_max, door_state}` (LY-10; the ask is closed, OQ-3). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **(orchestrator ruling; routed amendment to the Layout-side promise "every query is valid immediately after restore":)** leaves are derived by one `derive_doors` pass in Layout's `post_restore` (the kernel guarantees every `restore()` has completed before any `post_restore()` begins, KRN:843, so the Graph's persisted `area` is in memory whatever the order of the `post_restore` calls) and thereafter by `layout.doors`. Between `restore()` and `post_restore()` leaf-dependent queries (`rects_in`, `solid_in`, `clip_to_footprints`, `leaf_would_overlap`, `door_passage` (reports `open_extent_px` 0) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*) report the TEMPLATE default (every leaf closed) and raise a `stale_leaf` diagnostic flag if read. **Self-heal:** Layout's `post_restore` bumps `version(section_id)` (1 → 2) for every section whose derived leaf set differs from the all-closed template default; LY-12(d)'s "a restore is an unconditional rebuild signal" and the Emitter's W0 `version` read (EM:227) therefore rebuild the Emitter's static layer on tick 1 with no ordering between the two `post_restore` calls, and `body.integrate after: layout.doors` (LY-10) covers every P3 reader. Whether `post_restore` order follows `restore_after` is **informational only** (CR-8 and KRN:843 say "after every `restore()`"); no Layout rule depends on the answer. The `stale_leaf` diagnostic and this restore path are **live behaviour**, not a stand-in for an unanswered ask: they stay as specified now that the Graph read exists, because the window between `restore()` and `post_restore()` is real whatever the Graph publishes. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* `post_restore` also bumps `leaf_version` (never `static_version`) for each such section, and rebuilds the derived `opening_leaves` map from the restored `welds[]` and `seam_view(seam_id).opening_ids[]`.
(d) `post_restore()` does cross-block VERIFICATION only: every `graph_ref_base` resolves (node, edge and compartment counts match the template), every installed `def_id` at a hardpoint resolves in the Item DB catalogue (a diagnostic, not a hard fail), and every `welds[]` `seam_id` resolves to a Graph SeamRecord. Failures use the restore reason set (LY-29).
(e) *Template drift.* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The single `template_hash` is **split in two**, both persisted per instance (D.10): `geometry_hash` (u32; the canonical bytes of everything that decides where a rect, tile, socket, door or anchor is — room `origin_px` and tile runs, wall runs and the compiled rect table, socket `facing`/`line_px`/`start_px`/`width_tiles`/`hatch`, door positions and `area_max`, hardpoint cells, anchor polylines) and `visual_hash` (u32; kit-piece ids, art references, dialect, labels, hinted flags that no query reads). `restore` refuses an unknown `template_id` (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_UNKNOWN_TEMPLATE`) and a STRUCTURAL change (`LAYOUT_RESTORE_TEMPLATE_CHANGED`: the sets of `room_key`, `socket_key`, `hp_key`, `node_ref`, or any room's tile set differ) **and a geometry change on an instance that carries history** — `geometry_hash` differs and the instance has any non-`FREE` socket, any `welds[]` row naming it, or shares its body with another section — because a moved socket, wall edge or doorway under a welded or cut instance restores with broken abutment while every key set still matches (a socket position or wall rect edit used to classify as "visual-only"). A geometry change on a never-welded `FREE` instance alone is accepted with one diagnostic `geometry_changed_fresh` (nothing depends on it yet and its rects are re-derived from the new template); a `visual_hash` difference alone is accepted with one diagnostic. Pre-release saves are disposable (SL-14, adopted verbatim); after the first build given outside the project the migration obligation of LY-6(e) applies. `rot_q` must be 0 (LY-3 d).

**LY-27 — Mutators.** Layout has four mutators, all Class A (command-backed, validate-then-apply, CR-9) and **no Class B** (clamp-never-reject): it holds no quantity that can sensibly be clamped. Each has a pure `can_*` validate query; `apply` is infallible once validated (a failure inside `apply` is a defect and sends the kernel to `FAULTED`).
| LM1 | `build_section` | `template_id, kind` (`kind` forwarded to M1 only, never persisted); returns `{section_id, body_id}` | `can_build`: template known, Layout capacity (`MAX_SECTIONS`, `MAX_BODIES`, rooms, rects, **`MAX_DOORS_LOADED`** (loaded doors plus the template's doors; *added 2026-10-27 — re-review: the edge case 'refused earlier by `can_build` with `CAPACITY`' had no validate clause behind it*), **`next_section_id <= 2^20 − 1`**, the bound D.9's `rect_key` needs *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*), Graph `CAPACITY` pre-check | Web Map `init_world` (the only caller; a pod hop builds nothing) | `SEC/<id>`, `BODY/<id>` | Layout |
| `occluder_source(body_id)` → `rects_in(aabb, out)`, `version(section_id)`, `static_version(section_id)`, `leaf_version(section_id)` | records into the caller's `QueryBuffer`: `keys` (int64), occupied spans `(x0, y0, x1−1, y1−1)`, flags byte (LY-12 e); input `aabb` half-open | BODY | ascending key `(section_id, idx)` | `post_restore` (door leaves) | Layout *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: out-parameter, 64-bit keys, one convention)* |

**LY-31 — The PROJECTOR contract.** Layout's data module is scene-tree free (kernel H10): a headless test asserts it references no `Node`. A **separate PROJECTOR** (subscriber class `PROJECTOR`, CR-10: "write engine-side *derived* objects owned by its block owner … never writes blocks"; kernel example "Layout → physics projection; derelict content build") builds engine-side derived objects from `layout.state` and the templates (its scripts live in `src/presentation/projector/`, never in `src/sim/layout/`; ADR-0010 section 1.2) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0010 sync)*; they are never persisted and are rebuilt from the block, also after restore. The object shape (the [UNV] default and the weld spike that measures it) is in the engine feasibility note and ADR-LAY-03, not in this contract. It builds the door, prop and machinery sprites from the rect table and the seam bead, cap plate and scar pieces from `welds[]` and socket state. It fills the Pipeline's PR-5 layer stack (floor z 0 never Y-sorted, floor marks, ONE Y-sort `Node2D` holding in tree order wall-face, wall-mounted, doors, props, machinery, actors; wall caps) and gives every placed SPRITE object (door leaf, prop, machinery, bead or plate piece) the Pipeline's **`entity_id`** (PIPE D.12, PIPE:553: persistent, owned by the state block, stable across save and reload; the third key of `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)`, PIPE:1139). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `creation_id` is retired; the Pipeline has no such field.)* **Layout's `entity_id` (publisher-defined, G1; the namespace tag is registered with the Pipeline, Open Questions OQ-LY-ID):** a block-tagged int64, `entity_id = (LAYOUT_ID_NS << 56) | (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | template_local_idx`, with `LAYOUT_ID_NS` a Layout namespace byte in `1 … 127` (GDScript `int` is signed 64-bit, so a byte of 128 or more would make every Layout `entity_id` negative; the Pipeline compares ids as plain ints and only relative order inside one namespace matters, but the range is fixed so the sign is never in question) that Body, Interaction and any other id publisher must not use in its own high bits (so a Layout id can never equal a Body or Interaction id in the same `class_rank`), `section_id` 32 bits at most (`next_section_id` is monotonic and tombstones keep their ids), `kind_ordinal` 8 bits, `template_local_idx` 16 bits. It is a pure function of the block (`section_id`) and the template, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one, and it is never persisted by the PROJECTOR. **Tiles carry no `entity_id`:** `TileMapLayer` cells are not nodes; wall-face and cap tiles are `class_rank` 0 and tie-break among themselves by cell position `(y, x)` (the engine's own order for a `TileMapLayer`, Y-sort mechanism per SP-YSORT-1 below). Within `class_rank` 2 the doors, props and machinery of one `sort_y` are ordered by `entity_id` alone (they share one rank in the Pipeline; Layout assumes no sub-rank). The *mechanism* that delivers the key (`TileMapLayer` participation, who owns child insertion order) is not defined here and stays gated on SP-YSORT-1. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* It writes no block and creates **no engine tile collision and no navigation mesh in MVP**. It never creates `Light2D` or `LightOccluder2D` (Lighting's). Its section nodes are parented under Body's per-body root `Node2D` (Body's `body.projector` owns the root and its translation, BDY-33) — the default shape, which the Y-sort spike below may supersede with option B (no reparent; BDY-33 would then own the pose-driven section positions rather than a root). (→ ADR-LAY-03.) The PROJECTOR must satisfy "never hidden" (art bible 6.1) for seam beads. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Prerequisite story — the Y-sort / PROJECTOR scene-shape spike (SP-YSORT-1), done before the PROJECTOR story starts.** The default shape above reparents section nodes under a per-body root on every weld, which sits badly with the Pipeline's single Y-sort scope (PR-5: ONE Y-sort `Node2D` holding wall-face, wall-mounted, doors, props, machinery and actors in tree order) and is [UNV]. The spike tests **option B first**: *no reparent* — every section's nodes keep one parent under the single Y-sort node and each section's position is driven from the body's pose plus `section_offset` every tick (so a weld changes an offset, never a parent) — and falls back to option A (per-body roots, reparent on weld) only if B fails. **Exit criteria:** (1) the PR-5 draw order of AC-123 holds with two bodies in one scene and across a weld (an actor south of a wall over its face, north of it behind it, the cap above both); (2) no sprite changes sort rank across the weld frame; (3) draw calls for the MVP world are recorded for both options; (4) the weld frame costs at most one frame over the P99 ceiling (16.6 ms on RM-DESKTOP, 33.3 ms on RM-DECK; pending spike measurement) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)*; (5) the result is written to ADR-LAY-03. Until the spike closes, AC-140 has no pass line.

**LY-32 — Dirty keys and notification.** Layout's batch `(layout.state, tick, change_keys)` carries `SEC/<section_id>`, `BODY/<body_id>`, `S/<seam_id>`, or `ALL` past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256. **Encoding** (registry: `layout_dirty_key_encoding`)**:** Layout's keys are ints `(KIND << 32) | id` with KIND in {SEC 1, BODY 2, SEAM 3} (the Graph's LS-20 encoding, LSG:201), written in this document by family name; the family name `S/<seam_id>` is the Graph's (LS-20) and Failure & Trail's (FT:264, FT AC-107), so `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` accounting is comparable across blocks. Dirty keys are namespaced by block (CR-10; KRN:465 bounds them per block), so Layout's `SEC/<id>` and the Graph's `SEC/<id>` (LSG:170) are different keys in different blocks; every subscriber names the block, and subscribers that need both (Failure & Trail anchors, FT AC-107) subscribe to both.

### 1. The decisions at a glance

| Point (from the scope) | Decision | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Per-body roots | **Yes.** One `y_sort_enabled`, translation-only `BodyRoot` per body in the `ProjectionSet`, under one `y_sort_enabled` `World`. The root, not each node, carries the canvas offset. | § 2 |
| Reparent versus rebuild | **Reparent and recompute positions** for every moved section's nodes on weld and cut; **no tile is re-authored** (no `set_cell`, no chunked build), but **the engine rebuilds each moved `TileMapLayer`'s canvas items once, deferred** (V10), and that cost is charged to the weld budget. Re-authoring (chunked, staged, atomic) happens only on first build, arrival, restore, `ALL`, and a section whose template or discard state changed. `Staging` is a data stage only and does not pre-warm rendering. A fresh-build path stays the reference: a signature test requires both paths to give equal scenes, child order included. | § 7 |
| Per-body versus per-section `TileMapLayer` | **Per section**, one layer per layer kind (floor, wall face, mounted, cap), **exactly one `TileSetAtlasSource` each**. | § 5 |
| Y-sort key | `(sort_y, class_rank, entity_id)` realised as: engine key = integer node position (sprites) or `cell_top + tile_h/2 + origins` (tiles); class rank = group order; `entity_id` = child order of the sorted layers. Door and wall sort edges as in § 3. | § 3 |
| `entity_id` namespaces | `EntityId.pack(ns, local)` in `src/shared/`; namespace bytes **LAYOUT 1, BODY 2, INTERACTION 3, HORROR 4, SUIT 5, WEB 6, TRAIL 7, LIGHTING 8** (a registration key for attached lights, never a sort key), 9 to 127 reserved; the table is append-only with a golden test and is not an acceptance condition; Layout's local part as LY-31. | § 4 |
| Camera-limit rectangle | Integer base-px **raw hull rect** of the avatar's body: bounding box of `[offset, offset + size_tiles x TILE_PX)` over its sections, grown north by `WALL_FACE_PX + WALL_FOOTPRINT_DEPTH`, published as `CameraLimits` in stage `PROJECT`; `rect_eff`, the clamp order, `CLAMPED` and JOLT are ADR-0008's and the solver is the only clamp. | § 9 |
| SP-YSORT-1 | Confirms; does not choose. | § 11 |

### 4. `entity_id` and its namespaces

`entity_id` is **a presentation sort-key composite**, not a block id. It is a pure function of persisted ids, so it is identical in a live build and a restored one and is never stored. ADR-0003's rule (ids are block-local, cross-block references are `(block_id, entity_id)`) is unchanged.

```gdscript
# src/shared/entity_id.gd (L0: pure ints, no engine types; sim modules and presentation both may call it)
class_name EntityId extends RefCounted
const NS_SHIFT: int = 56
const LOCAL_MASK: int = (1 << 56) - 1
static func pack(ns: int, local: int) -> int           ## (ns << 56) | local; ns in 1..127; local in 0..LOCAL_MASK; asserts in debug, returns 0 (invalid) otherwise
static func ns_of(id: int) -> int
static func local_of(id: int) -> int
static func layout_local(section_id: int, kind_ordinal: int, idx: int) -> int   ## (section_id << 24) | (kind_ordinal << 16) | idx
# src/shared/entity_ns.gd : the namespace table (append-only; a golden test pins it)
class_name EntityNs extends RefCounted
const LAYOUT: int = 1       # door leaf, jamb, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar sprites
const BODY: int = 2         # actors (local = actor_id)
const INTERACTION: int = 3  # loose items, deployables (local = item_id)
const HORROR: int = 4       # horror rigs (local = horror entity_id)
const SUIT: int = 5         # empty suits and carried-and-dropped suit props
const WEB: int = 6          # off-floor web pieces
const TRAIL: int = 7        # trail sprites (local = the Graph subject key)
const LIGHTING: int = 8     # attached lights: a registration key for BodyScenes.attach_light (local = the seat's beam id); never a sort key
# 9..127: reserved, append-only (no renumbering, ever; a golden test pins the table)
```
- **The sign.** A namespace byte of 1 to 127 keeps every id positive in GDScript's signed 64-bit `int`, so ids compare as plain integers (the Pipeline never needs an unsigned compare). `0` is invalid.
- **Layout's local part** is LY-31's: `section_id` below `2^20` (ADR-0013 § 3 guarantees it), `kind_ordinal` in 8 bits, `idx` in 16 bits (the rect `idx` or the template placement index, below the rect stride, ADR-0013 § 13). **`kind_ordinal` ownership split (ruling CT-14).** ADR-0013 § 13 owns *which kinds* are in the closed vocabulary (door leaf, jamb, prop, machinery, bead, plate, scar: it adds `JAMB`); this ADR owns the *numbers*, assigned append-only by this section: `DOOR_LEAF 1`, `PROP 2`, `MACHINE 3`, `BEAD 4`, `PLATE 5`, `SCAR 6`, `JAMB 7` (TR-assembly-045 requires jambs; OQ-C closed). Class ranks: `BEAD`, `PLATE`, `SCAR` are rank 1 (the wall-mounted layer, LY-33); `DOOR_LEAF`, `JAMB`, `PROP`, `MACHINE` are rank 2. **Local `idx` of bead and scar sprites (T9d):** they come from `welds[]`, not from a template placement, and the seam is shared by two sections, so the rule is fixed: a bead or a scar uses the **reserved PLATE slot `idx` of the socket on the lower `section_id` side** of the seam, and **only that side's `SectionScene` builds it**. Two beads or a duplicate-id refusal therefore cannot occur; the other side builds none.
- **Other publishers' local parts** are their own persisted ids: Body's `actor_id` (an `int64` counter, asserted below `2^56`), Interaction's `item_id`, Horror's `entity_id`. Each publisher calls `EntityId.pack` itself; Layout exports no helper (ADR-0013 § 13), so the Layout projector packs, using only persisted ids.
- **Ordering consequence.** At an equal key and rank, namespaces order ascending: a Layout prop draws before an Interaction item, a Body actor before a horror. That is deterministic and save-stable; it is a convention, not a design claim.
- **Guard.** `SortedLayer.insert` refuses a duplicate `(class_rank, entity_id)`; a golden test pins the namespace table (append-only: a later ADR adopts its byte or requests an append, never a renumber, T6); a lint forbids `EntityId.pack` with a literal namespace outside `entity_ns.gd` (`PJT-08`). Registration of an attached node in `BodyScenes` is keyed by `(ns, local)` for every namespace; only the sorted groups use it as a sort key.

### 9. Mutators, checks, results, faults and dirty keys

Layout has **exactly four mutators, all Class A**, and no Class B (it holds no quantity that can sensibly be clamped) (TR-section-020). Each has a pure check; `apply` is infallible once its check passed and a failure inside it is a defect that returns `-fault_code` after `scope.fault`.

| # | Check (pure) | Mutator | Caller (one) | Results (caller-owned `out`) | Dirty keys |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| LM1 | `can_build(views, template_id, kind) -> StringName` | `build_section(scope, template_id, kind, out: BuildResult) -> int` | Web Map `init_world` in the `INIT` scope; a pod hop builds nothing | `section_id`, `body_id` | `SEC/<id>`, `BODY/<id>` |
| LM2 | `can_attach(views, socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b) -> StringName` | `attach_section(scope, socket_ref_a, socket_ref_b, seam_id, welded_at_T, out: AttachResult) -> int` | Assembly `weld` apply, after the Graph's `weld_join` | § 7 | `S/<seam_id>`, 2 x `BODY`, `SEC` per affected section |
| LM3 | `can_detach(views, seam_id) -> StringName` | `detach_section(scope, seam_id, boundary_mode, out: DetachResult) -> int` | Assembly `seam_cut` apply, after the Graph's `cut_detach` | § 7 | `S/<seam_id>`, `BODY/<kept>`, `BODY/<new>`, `SEC` per affected section (6 in D.12's example) |
| LM4 | `can_discard(views, section_id) -> StringName` | `discard_section_geometry(scope, section_id) -> int` | Web Map only, after the Graph's M4; Assembly never discards | none | `SEC/<id>`, `BODY/<id>` |

**LM4 and versions.** LM4 does not bump the three counters; it calls `LayoutVersions.invalidate(section_id)` (all three counters set to 0, ADR-0014 § 6), so a consumer's cached value can never equal a live one. **LM4 and Body (ruling CT-23):** discarding a section can dissolve its body, and Body has no implicit cleanup, so in the discard apply BM8 `release_body` must follow LM4 (assumption on ADR-0026, the discard apply order: BM5/BM2 move or remove actors, then Graph M4, then LM4, then BM8). **Records.** `BuildResult`, `AttachResult` and `DetachResult` are caller-owned and reused; each resets itself through a `reset()` method (not an `_init` re-run) before every Layout fill (§ 11, Key Interfaces).

**Naming divergence, recorded.** ADR-0003 § 5 and the registry give the check as `check_x(views, args) -> StringName`. The GDD, 19 TR rows and four consumer GDDs publish `can_build`, `can_attach`, `can_detach`, `can_discard`. This ADR keeps the **published names** and the **exact shape** (pure, takes `views` and scalars, returns `&""` for OK and a reason otherwise); the divergence is a prefix and is listed as an ask to ADR-0003 (§ Related). The GDD's "returns `{section_id, body_id}`" becomes an `out` record, as ADR-0003 requires for every mutator that produces data.

**Reasons (closed sets, StringNames in `LayoutReasons`).** `can_build`: `TEMPLATE_UNKNOWN`, `CAPACITY`; a refusal by the Graph's `check_instantiate_section` is passed through as `layout.GRAPH_<REASON>` (CAPACITY maps to `CAPACITY`; the LS-18 reasons and `ONSET_UNKEYED` surface as `GRAPH_<REASON>`, which is unreachable at runtime for a validated template because the ADR-0007 template validator calls `graph_rules.onset_valid` at boot). `can_attach`: the nine of § 6. `can_detach`: `SEAM_UNKNOWN`, `SEAM_NOT_ACTIVE`, `CAPACITY`. `can_discard`: `SECTION_UNKNOWN`, `SECTION_WELDED`. They surface as `VALIDATION_FAILED(layout.<REASON>)` in the kernel's existing channel. `BODY_FULL` and `OFFSET_OFF_GRID` are not added (§ Open Questions OQ-1).

**Capacity enforcement (TR-section-030, -037).** `can_build` returns `CAPACITY` when any of the following holds, evaluated before any id is consumed or the Graph is called: live sections `>= MAX_SECTIONS` (tombstones do not count); live bodies `>= MAX_BODIES`; `next_section_id > 2^20 - 1`; `next_body_id > 2^31 - 1`; `next_room_id + rooms - 1 > 2^31 - 1`; the template's rects exceed `MAX_FOOTPRINT_RECTS_PER_BODY` or its doors plus loaded doors exceed `MAX_DOORS_LOADED`; rooms exceed `MAX_ROOMS_PER_SECTION`; or the Graph's `check_instantiate_section` refuses (see Reasons). `can_detach` returns `CAPACITY` when a body cannot be allocated: live bodies `>= MAX_BODIES` or `next_body_id > 2^31 - 1`, so a cut at the ceiling is a clean reject in validate, never a `FAULTED` apply. `MAX_BODIES` is counted over `LIVE` bodies, with a welded home ship plus a welded derelict B counting as one (TR-derelict-040 Layout half). `BODIES_LIVE_MAX` (Lighting's) is **not** a Layout reject; beyond it Lighting degrades lights to stand-ins and the world lint `BODIES_LIVE_MARGIN` reports the zero MVP margin. The per-section and per-world limits (`MAX_DOORS_PER_SECTION`, `MAX_SOCKETS_PER_SECTION`, `MAX_HARDPOINTS_PER_SECTION`, `MAX_ANCHORS_PER_SECTION`, `MAX_LOOSE_SLOTS_PER_SECTION`) are boot invariants over a template (`CONTENT_INVARIANT`); the world tile ceiling `TILES_WORLD_MVP` and the Graph node/edge ceilings are lints (Layout supplies `V`).
